graft.title: Count Rust uses through qualified paths and macros
graft.need: drift calls relations unbacked that the code has: fully qualified calls without a `use` (`crate::linalg::matmul(...)` in src/stats/correlation.rs, `crate::simd::dot_kernel(...)` in src/linalg/schur.rs), a type in a signature (`crate::spectral::WindowSpec` in src/resample/poly.rs) and macro invocations (`crate::processor::forward_processor!(Echo)` in src/delay/mod.rs). In autodyne 20 of 147 declared relations read as unbacked this way. Intra-doc links in comments ((crate::dlpack::ForeignBuffer)) are rightly not uses.
graft.use_case: Keeping autodyne's declared relations and drift in agreement.

answer.text: Done in tend 9facf9e. (1) Test code apart: imports and name uses in a #[cfg(test)] module, a #[test] function (#[tokio::test] too) or a test file (tests/, tests.rs, *_test.rs, test_*.py, *.test.ts, *.spec.ts …) are counted on the code graph's edge as `test`. They still reach the code (for which tests reach a node), but drift no longer reads them as the design's uses. (2) Rust paths without a `use`: crate::/super::/self:: paths in calls, types and macro invocations count as uses of the module they name (through re-exports in mod.rs too); intra-doc links in comments aren't parsed, so they don't. They don't license method-name matching the way an import does. (3) A `raise NotImplementedError(...)` whose message names what's supported ('only', 'supports', 'unsupported', 'must be', 'one of' …, without 'yet' or 'not implemented'), or with a `# deliberate` comment on the line, isn't unfinished work. Caches move on, so the next drift recomputes.
